record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Shape function and exponent in fractal Weyl laws
record.original_question: What is the correct strip-width shape function f(C) in the fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic resonance spectra, and how can the fractal exponent ν be reliably checked in real scattering systems rather than only in simplified quantum-map models?

evidence.quote: An Ansatz for the “shape function” f (C) in (2) was proposed by Schomerus and Tworzydło, in terms of an ensemble of (subunitary) random matrices [29]; so far, the numerical data performed on quantum maps are not very conclusive.
Even numerically checking the exponent ν is a nontrivial task when one deals with a real scattering system [20].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open quantum chaotic system whose classical dynamics has a hyperbolic trapped set of fractal dimension, and let the quantum resonances (complex eigenvalues of the associated non-self-adjoint quantization, or eigenvalues of an open quantum map) be denoted by {z_j} in the unit disk (or in a strip below the real axis, in the scattering setting). The fractal Weyl law conjectures that, in the semiclassical limit ℏ → 0 (equivalently, dimension N → ∞ for an N-dimensional open quantum map), the number of resonances with imaginary part (or modulus, in the map setting) inside a strip of width C scales as

   #{ j : resonance z_j lies in a strip of width C } ~ f(C) · N^ν,

where ν is a fractal exponent expected to equal (d−1)/2 (or d, depending on convention) in terms of the fractal dimension d of the trapped set, and f(C) is a "shape function" describing the dependence on the strip width.

Problem. 
(a) Determine the correct shape function f(C) in this fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic resonance spectra. In particular, decide whether the random-matrix-theoretic Ansatz for f(C) obtained from an ensemble of subunitary random matrices is exact, asymptotically correct, or merely approximate, and identify the universal form of f(C).
(b) Provide a method to reliably verify (numerically or theoretically) the fractal exponent ν in genuine scattering systems (e.g. Hamiltonian flows with several convex obstacles, or three-dimensional scattering Hamiltonians), rather than only in simplified quantum-map toy models.
artifact.category_tag: Fractal Weyl laws and quantum resonances
artifact.status_search_result: The fractal Weyl law remains an active research topic. Rigorous upper bounds of fractal Weyl type for open quantum chaotic maps have been established (Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski, Annals of Math. 2014), but matching lower bounds and the exact form of the shape function f(C) are not established in general. Recent work (e.g. arXiv:2512.03773, "Counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for semiclassical resonances") indicates that the conjectured law can fail in some semiclassical settings, and numerical verification of the exponent ν in real scattering systems remains difficult. Thus the question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open quantum chaotic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous fractal Weyl upper bounds for open quantum maps with hyperbolic trapped set.
status_evidence.claim: Only upper bounds are proven; matching shape and lower bound remain open.

status_evidence.title: Counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law for semiclassical resonances
status_evidence.snippet: Recent counter-examples to the fractal Weyl law in semiclassical resonance settings.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured fractal Weyl law is not universally valid, indicating the question of the correct shape and exponent in real scattering systems remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Fractal Weyl law for open chaotic maps (arXiv:1105.3128)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of fractal Weyl laws for open quantum chaotic maps.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical verification of the exponent in true scattering systems is still a nontrivial open problem.
